report_name: Judge Approves $117.5M Settlement in Comcast 'Citrix Bleed' Breach

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: Threat actors exploited the 'Citrix Bleed' vulnerability (CVE-2023-4966) on Comcast's public-facing Citrix NetScaler appliances to gain initial access.

attack_patterns.name: Modify Authentication Process: Multi-Factor Authentication
attack_patterns.description: Attackers replayed stolen session tokens to bypass password and multi-factor authentication (MFA), a form of modifying the authentication process.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Stolen session tokens were replayed to hijack legitimate user sessions, granting attackers access as if they were the valid user.

attack_patterns.name: External Remote Services
attack_patterns.description: The attack vector involved exploiting Citrix NetScaler appliances, which are considered external remote services.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2023-4966
vulnerabilities.description: A critical vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances, also known as 'Citrix Bleed', that allowed unauthenticated attackers to retrieve sensitive session tokens from memory. This was exploited against Comcast between October 16 and October 19, 2023.

identities.name: Comcast Cable Communications
identities.description: Victim of a data breach in October 2023 affecting 31.7 million customers due to the exploitation of the Citrix Bleed vulnerability (CVE-2023-4966). The company reached a $117.5 million settlement in a resulting class-action lawsuit.

identities.name: Citrix
identities.description: Vendor of the NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances that contained the 'Citrix Bleed' (CVE-2023-4966) vulnerability.
